selector.rationale: The patient presented with acute abdominal pain, peritonism, and a perforated appendix, which led to sepsis due to four-quadrant purulent contamination.

rejected.label: Lymphoma
rejected.why: Although lymphadenopathy was present, it was not the primary cause of the patient's acute presentation.

rejected.label: Metastatic prostate cancer
rejected.why: The patient's prostate cancer was in remission, and the current symptoms were not directly related to cancer.

rejected.label: Acute respiratory distress syndrome (ARDS)
rejected.why: While the patient had pulmonary consolidation and required ventilation, ARDS was a secondary complication rather than the primary diagnosis.

rejected.label: Appendicitis
rejected.why: Although the patient had appendicitis, it is not the champion diagnosis because sepsis was the more severe and life-threatening condition that developed as a result of the appendicitis.
